title: Default hardcoded auth secret baked into Docker image (NEXTAUTH_SECRET=secret)
description: Cross-layer correlation of the root Dockerfile default build-arg secret ARG NEXTAUTH_SECRET=secret (L11), baked into ENV (L29). Detected by L1 architectural review (secrets-management, CWE-798 use of hardcoded credentials) and by L3b cross-file taint (the value flows to next-auth JWT/session signing via getToken({req,secret}) in apps/api/v2/src/modules/auth/strategies/api-auth/api-auth.strategy.ts, CWE-347), enabling session/JWT forgery and auth bypass if an image is built without overriding the arg. L2 (Semgrep CE p/secrets) did not independently enumerate this Dockerfile default because the literal 'secret' is a low-entropy value below single-file SAST secret-detection thresholds; this is precisely the intra-file limitation the L3b agent taint layer exists to compensate for (AAP 0.1.1). The companion default ARG CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY=secret (Dockerfile L12) is tracked as a separate merged finding.

title: API v2 Dockerfile runs container as root (no USER directive)
description: Cross-layer correlation at apps/api/v2/Dockerfile L26: the NestJS image (FROM node:20-alpine, EXPOSE 80) launches its CMD without ever declaring a USER, so the API server runs as UID 0. Independently detected by L1 architectural review (container-security, CWE-250) and by L2 Semgrep (rule dockerfile.security.missing-user, p/owasp-top-ten). Merged severity is high (L2 gate-blocking assessment prevails over L1's medium defense-in-depth rating). Add a dedicated non-root user before the CMD to reduce blast radius of a container compromise.

title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML on team bio (server-sanitized) in team-view.tsx
description: Cross-layer correlation at apps/web/modules/team/team-view.tsx L161: user-provided team bio is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Detected by L2 Semgrep (react-dangerouslysetinnerhtml, p/security-audit, CWE-79) and by L3b taint, which traces the source to team.safeBio and confirms server-side HTML sanitization is applied (mitigation_present; output-sanitization inventory=4). Residual risk is medium and non-gate-blocking given the sanitization control.

title: Suppressed: fast-xml-parser 4.4.1 advisories (npm audit 1113407) via @aws-sdk/core
description: Cross-layer correlation of the documented advisory suppression. L1 architectural review flags the .yarnrc.yml npmAuditIgnoreAdvisories entry '1113407' for fast-xml-parser 4.4.1 (transitive via @boxyhq/saml-jackson -> @aws-sdk/core), and L4 OSV-Scanner enumerates the underlying advisories (collapsed here: L4-087, L4-088, L4-089, L4-090, L4-091, L4-092). The parser only handles trusted AWS API responses (not user input) and an upstream fix is pending; the suppression is documented and justified in-file. Treated as accepted, documented risk: suppressed=true, gate_blocking=false. Note: fast-xml-parser 5.3.5 advisories are a different installed version, are NOT covered by advisory 1113407, and remain active (non-suppressed) merged findings.

title: Root Dockerfile runs container as root (no USER directive)
description: The root Dockerfile defines three build stages (builder, builder-two, runner) but never declares a USER directive, so the final runner image and its entrypoint execute with UID 0 (root). A container escape or RCE in the Node process therefore runs with root privileges inside the container. Best practice is to add a non-root USER in the runner stage (CWE-250 execution with unnecessary privileges).  Evidence: FROM node:20 AS runner ... CMD ['/calcom/scripts/start.sh'] (no USER directive in any of the 3 stages)

title: GitHub Action pinned to mutable tag instead of commit SHA
description: The security-audit workflow references actions/checkout@v4, a mutable tag that a compromised or re-tagged upstream release could repoint to malicious code executed inside CI with repository credentials. This unpinned-action pattern generalizes across the repository's 59 workflow files. Pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA (CWE-1357 reliance on insufficiently trustworthy component).  Evidence: - uses: actions/checkout@v4

title: Concrete hardcoded CRON_API_KEY committed in .env template
description: The committed environment template contains a realistic 32-hex-character secret value for CRON_API_KEY rather than an empty placeholder. Operators who copy .env.example to .env verbatim will ship a publicly known cron API key that authenticates privileged cron endpoints, allowing unauthorized job invocation (CWE-798 use of hardcoded credentials).  Evidence: CRON_API_KEY='REDACTED_CRON_API_KEY'

title: Wildcard CORS origin permitted in non-production only
description: enableCors() resolves its origin to the wildcard * as the final fallback, but only when ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset AND NODE_ENV is not production (production defaults to false, i.e. CORS disabled). The wildcard is therefore confined to local/dev convenience and does not weaken production, so severity is low; operators should still set ALLOWED_ORIGINS explicitly (CWE-942 permissive cross-domain policy).  Evidence: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? false : '*'

title: CSP script-src allows 'unsafe-inline' (prod fallback) and 'unsafe-eval' (dev)
description: getCspPolicy() emits a production script-src containing 'unsafe-inline' https: (alongside a per-request nonce and 'strict-dynamic') and a development script-src containing 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https: http:. The unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval tokens weaken XSS protection; they are a documented browser-compat fallback and are partially neutralized by 'strict-dynamic' in supporting browsers. Strong compensating controls exist (nonce, strict-dynamic, object-src 'none', base-uri 'none'), so severity is medium (CWE-1021/CWE-79).  Evidence: 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic' 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https:

title: Global static CSP header allows 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' scripts
description: The Next.js headers() config sets a static Content-Security-Policy for source /:path* whose script-src permits 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https:. Unlike the nonce-based edge CSP, this header applies to all matched routes in every environment and permits inline script and eval(), materially weakening XSS defense. Compensating directives (frame-ancestors 'self', base-uri 'self', form-action 'self') limit but do not remove the risk (CWE-79).  Evidence: script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https:

title: API v1 accepts API key via URL query string
description: The v1 API middleware reads the caller's API key from req.query.apiKey. Secrets placed in URLs can leak through server/proxy access logs, browser history, and Referer headers (CWE-598 use of GET request with sensitive query strings). Risk is reduced because the key is immediately hashed via hashAPIKey() before any DB lookup and the modern v2 strategy uses a Bearer Authorization header plus sha256Hash, so severity is low.  Evidence: const strippedApiKey = `${req.query.apiKey}`.replace(process.env.API_KEY_PREFIX || 'cal_', '')

title: Default Postgres service credentials in docker-compose
description: The database service hardcodes default credentials POSTGRES_USER=unicorn_user (L20) and POSTGRES_PASSWORD=magical_password (L21). These well-known defaults would grant DB access to anyone who can reach the service. Exposure is limited because the database service publishes no host port and lives on the internal stack network (external: false); however the optional Prisma Studio service exposes port 5555 with only a documented prod-removal warning (L120). Operators must override these before any non-local deployment (CWE-798/CWE-1188).  Evidence: POSTGRES_USER=unicorn_user / POSTGRES_PASSWORD=magical_password

title: weak-hash
description: Source: hardcoded default build arg CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY=secret. Sink: aes256 symmetricEncrypt / createCipheriv key material. Dockerfile ARG CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY=secret (L12) -> ENV CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (L30) -> at-rest credential encryption key consumed by packages/lib/crypto.ts createCipheriv('aes256', key) (L18). Guessable default weakens stored-credential confidentiality; lower impact than session forgery (requires datastore access), so medium and non-gate-blocking. Production deployments must override. Mitigation: none (production override required). Exploitability: exploitable.

title: weak-hash
description: Source: attacker-supplied x-vercel-signature header. Sink: crypto.createHmac('sha1', secret). Inbound header x-vercel-signature -> HMAC-SHA1 verification (L44). SHA-1 inside an HMAC construction is not affected by SHA-1 collision weakness and remains cryptographically acceptable; comparison is guarded by crypto.timingSafeEqual (L53) preventing timing leaks. Mitigation: timingSafeEqual (constant-time-compare). Exploitability: mitigated.

title: weak-hash
description: Source: internal symmetric-encryption API (no external source). Sink: createCipheriv('aes256', ...). Legacy 'aes256' (AES-256-CBC) cipher uses a per-message crypto.randomBytes IV (L17, strong RNG); modern code paths use authenticated AES-256-GCM via packages/lib/crypto/keyring.ts. Algorithm is legacy/informational, not broken, and has no user-controlled taint source. Mitigation: randomBytes IV; AES-256-GCM keyring available. Exploitability: non-exploitable.

title: ssrf
description: Source: webhook.subscriberUrl (admin/tenant-configured). Sink: fetch(subscriberUrl). Admin/tenant-configured subscriberUrl -> outbound fetch() POST (L373). Delivery is HMAC-signed (X-Cal-Signature-256 via createHmac('sha256'), L349) and uses redirect:'manual' (L376). Destination is not anonymous-user-controlled; classified mitigated unless a specific unauthenticated user-controlled fetch target is proven. Mitigation: HMAC signature + redirect:manual + admin-config. Exploitability: mitigated.

title: template-ssti
description: Source: webhook.payloadTemplate (admin-configured). Sink: handlebars.compile(template). Admin-configured payloadTemplate -> handlebars.compile (L28) -> applyTemplate (L216). Handlebars is logic-less and the template originates from privileged configuration, not anonymous user input; no arbitrary code execution path. Mitigation: admin-only config; logic-less Handlebars. Exploitability: mitigated.

title: weak-prng
description: Source: UI rendering (no security decision). Sink: Math.random(). Math.random() drives UI skeleton bar heights and React key fallbacks (non-security). Security-sensitive randomness uses CSPRNGs: crypto.getRandomValues for the CSP nonce (apps/web/lib/csp.ts L39) and crypto.randomBytes for GCM nonces/IVs (packages/lib/crypto/keyring.ts L86). Mitigation: crypto.getRandomValues/randomBytes on security paths. Exploitability: non-exploitable.

title: sql-injection
description: Source: bulk event-type update values (server-constructed). Sink: tx.$executeRawUnsafe(sqlQuery, ...parameters). The sole $executeRawUnsafe in application code (L265) passes values as bound ...parameters rather than string interpolation; all other raw SQL uses Prisma $queryRaw tagged templates which auto-parameterize. No user-controlled string is concatenated into SQL. Mitigation: parameterized query (bound parameters). Exploitability: mitigated.

title: open-redirect
description: Source: route param bookingUid / request URL. Sink: NextResponse.redirect. Redirect destination is built as an internal path new URL('/booking/'+bookingUid, request.url) (L106) resolving same-origin; the user cannot control an absolute external destination. Pervasive Zod input-validation (=1017) guards route inputs. Mitigation: internal path construction; Zod input-validation. Exploitability: mitigated.

title: command-injection
description: Source: build/CI tooling (constant arguments). Sink: execSync / spawnSync. child_process usages are confined to build/CI/devtools scripts (docker-start.ts L5, apps/api/v2/src/swagger/generate-swagger.ts L35, apps/web/scripts/ts-check-changed-files.ts) invoking constant/hardcoded commands. No runtime request handler or anonymous-user source reaches these sinks. Mitigation: n/a (build-time only; no user-controlled source). Exploitability: non-exploitable.

title: path-traversal
description: Source: static template filename (no user segment). Sink: readFileSync(path.join(...)). path.join(emailsDir, 'confirm-email.html') (L25) joins a constant filename under an internal directory; remaining matches are build-time CLI traversal (packages/app-store-cli). No user-controlled path segment reaches the filesystem sink. Mitigation: n/a (constant/internal paths; no user source). Exploitability: non-exploitable.

title: prototype-pollution
description: Source: server-derived objects (no attacker-controlled keys). Sink: Object.assign({}, ...). Object.assign merges server-derived banner objects into a fresh {} target (L25); other matches merge constant style objects or are Zod schema .merge() calls. No attacker-controlled key (e.g. __proto__) flows into a shared prototype. Mitigation: fresh target object; non-user-controlled keys. Exploitability: non-exploitable.

title: redos
description: Source: eventLocationType.urlRegExp (trusted app-store config). Sink: new RegExp(dynamic). new RegExp(urlRegExp) (L44) is built from trusted app-store location-type configuration and wrapped in Zod string validation; other new RegExp sites use constant patterns. No anonymous-user-supplied pattern reaches the regex compiler. Mitigation: trusted app-store config; Zod validation. Exploitability: mitigated.

title: insecure-cookie
description: Source: server-generated slot-reservation uid. Sink: res.cookie('uid', uid). res.cookie('uid', uid) (L129) sets a short-lived, non-session slot-reservation hold that carries no authentication or sensitive material; session cookies are issued by next-auth with secure defaults. Absence of explicit Secure/HttpOnly on this non-sensitive cookie is low impact. Mitigation: non-session cookie; next-auth secure session cookies. Exploitability: non-exploitable.

title: xxe
description: Source: rich-text editor HTML (client-side). Sink: new DOMParser().parseFromString. The single xxe candidate uses the browser WHATWG DOMParser (L371, also L394) to parse editor HTML client-side. DOMParser does not resolve external entities and there is no server-side XML entity expansion, so XXE is not applicable. Mitigation: browser DOMParser (no external-entity resolution). Exploitability: non-exploitable.
